newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse closes off record highs.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse closes off record highs.

text.p: German shares ended bourse dealings lower on Wednesday, taking a breather after their record-breaking rally the day before and discouraged by weakness on foreign markets.
But dealers said the market had been supported by strength in the German bond market.

The DAX index of 30 leading shares closed floor trade down 13.61 points, or 0.48 percent, at 2,797.03, not managing to hold above the crucial 2,800 point level, which it had managed to penetrate decisively for the first time on Tuesday.

German Bund strength had been supportive for the market in early dealings as the December Bund future made an all-time high of 101.55. But the contract later pared gains to around trade aroung 101.46.

Shares in Europe's largest carmaker Volkswagen AG were in the spotlight, slipping almost six percent, or 37.70 marks to 601.25 marks in bourse trade, after a U.S. judge denied VW's motion to dismiss racketeering claims by rival Opel.
The ruling could open VW to potentially higher damages in the lawsuit with Opel, a subsidiary of U.S. carmaker General Motors.
VW shares were also under pressure after the firm said it could introduce short-time working hours at its main plant because a French truck blockade has hit the supply of car parts.
Shares in other German car makers were also weaker than the trend, BMW AG down nine marks at 976 marks and Daimler-Benz AG off 1.23 marks at 98.65 marks.

Meanwhile, shares in diversified group Veba AG were firmer, rising 41 pfennigs to 89.08 marks after the group said it plans to create 15,000 jobs in the coming year, mainly in its telecommunications division.
